title: Toronto officer cleared of wrongdoing in shooting death
subtitle: The SIU has cleared a Toronto police officer of wrongdoing after he shot and killed a machete-wielding suspect last fall.
article: The SIU has cleared a Toronto police officer of wrongdoing after he shot and killed a machete-wielding suspect last fall.
The Special Investigations Unit was called in after an incident on Oct. 23, 2010 that left 28-year-old Amit Krishna of Toronto dead.

The arm's-length agency - which investigates instances of serious injury, death or sexual assault involving police - concluded there were no grounds to lay criminal charges against any of the officers involved in the violent struggle that led to Krishna's death.

According to an SIU statement released Tuesday, two police officers went to Krishna's apartment at 200 Dufferin St. just south of King St. W. to arrest him on an outstanding warrant. Once inside, they found him in total darkness in his bedroom and brought him into the living room.

The officers asked if he wanted to change his clothes and followed him back to his bedroom. Krishna then appeared to reach into a bag to pull out clothing but instead produced a machete knife and lunged at one of the officers.

Krishna struggled with the officer and landed a "glancing blow" to the side of his head with the knife. The second officer, the subject of the SIU's investigation, opened fire on Krishna, according to the statement.
A post-mortem exam revealed he died of multiple gunshot wounds.
SIU director Ian Scott said the officer's use of lethal force was justified.

"[H]e saw the witness officer in immediate jeopardy of grievous injury or death as a result of the knife attack by Mr. Krishna. Accordingly, the subject officer was justified in responding with the use of his firearm, causing the death of Mr. Krishna," Scott said in the statement.

The SIU assigned five investigators and three forensic investigators to look into the incident. They interviewed a number of witnesses who were in the apartment at the time of the shooting as well as several police officers.
Neither of the officers involved was named in the SIU's statement.
